channel.title: Auto Research Digest EN RSS
channel.description: A research publication on the design, approval, evaluation, and operation of LLMs, generative AI, and AI agents in real work.

item.title: When can a human approval become a rule for future agent tasks?
item.description: An invoice example explains when AI agents can reuse human approvals, with explicit conditions, exception tests, rule ownership, and expiry.

item.title: When to clarify a request and when to show an AI prototype
item.description: Use questions for missing requirements and prototypes for emerging preferences. Research and an outline example explain revision and verification.

item.title: Evaluating AI agent actions beyond the final answer
item.description: Evaluate AI agents using booking traces, approval order, tool arguments, and saved state. Learn how to allow valid paths and detect regressions.

item.title: Verifying AI data entry and saves in applications without APIs
item.description: Verify computer-use agents before and after Save. An invoice example covers duplicate prevention, managed desktops, and uncertain results.

item.title: What to verify when sales AI turns meeting notes into CRM updates
item.description: Check CRM update proposals from sales AI: opportunity matching, field evidence, changed records, and saved results, with product comparisons.

item.title: Choosing editable formats for AI-generated presentations
item.description: Compare images, SVGs, and chart objects in AI-generated slides, then test the next revision in PowerPoint or Google Slides.

item.title: How to compare permissions, approvals, and evaluation in agent platforms
item.description: Use a ticket-update task to compare agent platform permissions, approvals, traces, and evaluation, including responsibilities left to existing systems.

item.title: From an agent listing to an approved organizational trial
item.description: Separate agent discovery, connection, purchase, and distribution. Define permissions, costs, changes, and withdrawal for an organizational trial.

item.title: What to preserve so an AI agent can resume interrupted work
item.description: Distinguish saved sessions from task recovery using Managed Agents and Google ADK: persistence, artifact versions, duplicate actions, and resumption checks.

item.title: Reviewing a coding agent: plans, permissions, diffs, and tests
item.description: Separate coding-agent plan review, branch and VM isolation, Verified signatures, and test evidence to understand what each check establishes.

item.title: AI agent memory is shifting from vector retrieval to a layered systems design
item.description: Using primary sources from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google ADK and others, this briefing explains why agent memory is moving from one-shot retrieval to layered memory design.

item.title: Voice AI agents are shifting from demo features to operational systems
item.description: From public material by OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and AWS, this article outlines how voice agents are moving from demo features into operational systems.

item.title: Subagents are becoming the practical implementation unit for real-world AI work
item.description: Using public material from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and AWS, this briefing explains why subagents are becoming a practical unit of AI implementation.

item.title: MCP, A2A, and AG-UI are separating the connection stack for AI agents
item.description: Using protocol specifications and vendor docs, this briefing explains how MCP, A2A, and AG-UI are separating tool access, delegation, and human approval layers.

item.title: How practical video generation AI has become: the latest product status and technology shifts across five major platforms
item.description: Comparing OpenAI, Google, Adobe, Runway, and Luma, this article maps where video generation AI is becoming practical and where limits still matter.

item.title: Agent identity is becoming the control plane for authentication and authorization
item.description: Across primary sources from Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Okta, and Auth0, this article explains why agent identity is becoming an auth control plane.

item.title: Cowork signals that workplace AI is expanding into long-running agent systems
item.description: Using material from Anthropic, Microsoft, Google, Slack, and OpenAI, this article maps the shift toward long-running workplace agent systems.

item.title: Why generative AI products converge on chat, and why chat will not stay alone
item.description: Across OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, and Anthropic product signals, this article explains why AI products converge on chat but do not stop there.

item.title: Security gates are becoming part of the core comparison axis for AI agents
item.description: Using primary-source material from OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, AWS, and Google Cloud, this piece explains why security gates now shape agent comparison.

item.title: AI agent adoption is shifting from model races to operational architecture
item.description: Using major research and platform docs from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and AWS, this article maps the shift toward operational architecture.
